cards.headline:
층을 망가뜨린 언어 모델
뇌졸중 실어증 닮아
cards.body: 대형 언어 모델의 층을 망가뜨리자 뇌졸중 뒤 실어증 같은 오류가 나왔다.

blocks.cap: 사진: Pixabay/CC0 Public Domain

blocks.x: 연구자들은 150년 넘게 손상이 행동 결함을 어떻게 일으키는지 살피며 뇌 지도를 그려 왔다. 뇌졸중 뒤 언어·말하기 장애를 전문으로 연구하는 한 팀은 이 틀을 대형 언어 모델에도 쓸 수 있다고 말한다.

University of South Carolina의 Julius Fridriksson 연구팀은 Patterns에 실린 연구에서 "언어 모델의 층을 교란"한 뒤 환자에게 쓰는 임상 검사를 똑같이 해 볼 수 있는지 물었다. 이 연구실은 뇌졸중 환자의 뇌 영상으로 실어증을 연구한다. Fridriksson은 "LLMs는 실패가 대가를 치르는 상황에 배치되고 있다"고 말한다.
일부러 만든 "병변"은 연구팀이 보는 실어증 환자와 비슷한 언어 오류를 냈다. 공동 저자 Roger Newman-Norlund는 모델이 사람처럼 언어·인지·이해 오류를 보인다고 말한다. Fridriksson은 이 접근법이 "인과관계를 확립한다"면서도, 논문이 보여 주는 건 실제 구조가 아니라 실패 패턴의 대응이라고 짚는다.

연구팀은 병변 기반 해석 가능성이 LLM의 "블랙박스"를 열어 불필요한 부분을 찾는 데 쓰이면 더 작고 에너지 효율 높은 모델로 이어질 수 있다고 말한다. 실어증 환자의 "디지털 트윈"을 만들어 임상시험을 시뮬레이션할 수도 있다. Fridriksson은 이 틀을 다른 신경 질환으로 넓힐 수 있다고 본다. "이 접근법이 받아들여져 환자에게 도움이 되는 과학적 발견으로 이어지길 바란다."

en.headline:
Lesioned language models
show stroke-like aphasia
en.body: Damaging layers of large language models produced error patterns resembling human aphasia after stroke.

blocks.cap: Credit: Pixabay/CC0 Public Domain

blocks.x: For more than 150 years, researchers have mapped the brain by studying how injuries cause behavioral deficits. A team specializing in post-stroke language and speech difficulties says the same framework can be applied to large language models.

In a study in Patterns, the team led by Julius Fridriksson of the University of South Carolina, whose lab studies aphasia using brain imaging of stroke patients, asked whether they could "perturb layers in the language model" and give it the same clinical tests used on patients. "LLMs are being deployed in situations where failure has consequences," Fridriksson says.

The deliberately introduced "lesions" produced language errors resembling those of their aphasia patients. Coauthor Roger Newman-Norlund says the models make language, cognition and comprehension errors similar to humans'. Fridriksson says the approach "establishes cause and effect," while noting the paper shows correspondence in failure patterns, not in actual structures.

The researchers say lesion-based interpretability could help open the LLM "black box" and identify redundant parts, leading to smaller, more energy-efficient models, and could create "digital twins" of aphasia patients to simulate clinical trials. Fridriksson believes the framework could extend to other neurological conditions: "I hope this approach will be embraced to make scientific discoveries that help patients."

ja.headline:
損傷させた言語モデル
脳卒中型の失語を示す
ja.body: 大規模言語モデルの層を損傷させると、脳卒中後の人の失語症に似た誤りのパターンが現れた。

blocks.cap: 提供：Pixabay/CC0 Public Domain

blocks.x: 研究者は150年以上にわたり、損傷が行動の障害をどう引き起こすかを調べることで脳の地図を描いてきた。脳卒中後の言語・発話障害を専門とするチームは、同じ枠組みを大規模言語モデルにも適用できるという。
Patternsに掲載された研究で、University of South CarolinaのJulius Fridriksson率いるチーム（同氏の研究室は脳卒中患者の脳画像を使って失語症を研究している）は、「言語モデルの層をかき乱し」、患者と同じ臨床検査を受けさせられるかを問うた。「LLMsは失敗が重大な結果を招く場面に導入されつつある」とFridrikssonは言う。
意図的に加えた「病変」は、チームが診る失語症患者と似た言語の誤りを生んだ。共著者のRoger Newman-Norlundは、モデルが人間と似た言語・認知・理解の誤りを犯すと述べる。Fridrikssonはこの手法が「因果関係を確立する」とする一方、論文が示すのは実際の構造ではなく失敗パターンの対応だと指摘する。
研究チームによれば、病変に基づく解釈可能性はLLMの「ブラックボックス」を開き、冗長な部分を特定する助けとなり、より小さく省エネなモデルにつながりうる。また失語症患者の「デジタルツイン」を作り、臨床試験をシミュレーションすることもできるという。Fridrikssonはこの枠組みが他の神経疾患にも広がりうると考える。「この手法が受け入れられ、患者を助ける科学的発見につながることを願う」

zh.headline:
受损的语言模型
出现类似中风的失语
zh.body: 破坏大语言模型的层后，模型出现了类似人类中风后失语症的错误模式。

blocks.cap: 图片来源：Pixabay/CC0 Public Domain

blocks.x: 150多年来，研究人员一直通过研究损伤如何导致行为缺陷来绘制大脑图谱。一支专攻中风后语言和言语障碍的团队表示，同样的框架也可用于大语言模型。
在发表于Patterns的研究中，University of South Carolina的Julius Fridriksson带领团队提出疑问：能否“扰动语言模型中的层”，再让它接受与患者相同的临床测试。他的实验室利用中风患者的脑成像研究失语症。Fridriksson说：“LLMs正被部署在失败会带来后果的场景中。”
刻意引入的“病灶”产生了与团队失语症患者相似的语言错误。共同作者Roger Newman-Norlund表示，这些模型会犯与人类相似的语言、认知和理解错误。Fridriksson称这一方法“确立了因果关系”，同时指出论文展示的是失败模式上的对应，而非实际结构上的对应。
研究人员表示，基于病灶的可解释性有助于打开LLM的“黑箱”，找出冗余部分，从而做出更小、更节能的模型，还可以创建失语症患者的“数字孪生”来模拟临床试验。Fridriksson认为该框架可扩展到其他神经系统疾病：“我希望这种方法能被采纳，用来做出帮助患者的科学发现。”

es.headline:
Modelos de lenguaje lesionados
muestran afasia similar a ictus
es.body: Dañar capas de grandes modelos de lenguaje produjo patrones de error parecidos a la afasia humana tras un ictus.

blocks.cap: Crédito: Pixabay/CC0 Public Domain

blocks.x: Durante más de 150 años, los investigadores han cartografiado el cerebro estudiando cómo las lesiones causan déficits conductuales. Un equipo especializado en trastornos del lenguaje y del habla tras un ictus afirma que el mismo marco puede aplicarse a los grandes modelos de lenguaje.

En un estudio publicado en Patterns, el equipo dirigido por Julius Fridriksson, de la University of South Carolina, cuyo laboratorio estudia la afasia mediante imágenes cerebrales de pacientes con ictus, se preguntó si podía "perturbar capas del modelo de lenguaje" y aplicarle las mismas pruebas clínicas que a los pacientes. "Los LLMs se están desplegando en situaciones donde los fallos tienen consecuencias", dice Fridriksson.

Las "lesiones" introducidas deliberadamente produjeron errores de lenguaje parecidos a los de sus pacientes con afasia. El coautor Roger Newman-Norlund señala que los modelos cometen errores de lenguaje, cognición y comprensión similares a los humanos. Fridriksson afirma que el enfoque "establece causa y efecto", aunque advierte que el artículo muestra una correspondencia en los patrones de fallo, no en las estructuras reales.

Los investigadores dicen que la interpretabilidad basada en lesiones podría ayudar a abrir la "caja negra" de los LLM e identificar partes redundantes, lo que llevaría a modelos más pequeños y eficientes en energía, y podría crear "gemelos digitales" de pacientes con afasia para simular ensayos clínicos. Fridriksson cree que el marco podría extenderse a otras afecciones neurológicas: "Espero que este enfoque se adopte para hacer descubrimientos científicos que ayuden a los pacientes".

cards.headline:
바이브 고고학 헛발질
과학계 AI 논쟁 불러
cards.body: AI 에이전트가 마야 유적을 찾았다는 주장은 틀렸지만 과학계 AI 논쟁을 낳았다.

en.headline:
A Maya site, 'vibe archaeology'
and a fight over AI in science
en.body: AI agents did not discover the Maya site, yet the viral claim sparked a clash over how AI should be used in science.

blocks.cap: The previously documented ancient Maya site. Estrada-Belli et al., Journal of Archaeological Science: Reports, Vol. 66; October 2025

blocks.x: On November 10 AI researcher Pietro Miotti shared on X what appeared to be a previously unmapped ancient Maya civic center in Mexico, found by prompting dozens of AI agents to sift through public NASA lidar data. The post went viral as "vibe archaeology," boosted by accounts including Polymarket.

But the site wasn't a new discovery. Less than a day later, Sarah Parcak of the University of Alabama at Birmingham noted it had been documented by Tulane's Francisco Estrada-Belli and colleagues in 2025. "This is why peer review exists," Parcak says. "Not everything is online."

“I think it’s great that people want to be citizen scientists using AI and experiment with it,” Estrada-Belli says. “But I think they shouldn’t just blindly take the results without doing some background checks or due diligence before they go out and make a claim like that.”

Miotti corrected his posts to credit the survey. "Today a single person with a hypothesis can run AI agents overnight to triage candidate structures for experts to evaluate," he says, adding that the episode showed the human contribution: "literature review, field verification and other more specific domain expertise."

es.headline:
Sitio maya, 'arqueología vibe'
y una pugna por la IA en ciencia
es.body: Los agentes de IA no hallaron el sitio maya, pero la afirmación viral abrió un debate sobre el uso científico de la IA.

blocks.cap: El antiguo sitio maya ya documentado. Estrada-Belli et al., Journal of Archaeological Science: Reports, Vol. 66; October 2025

blocks.x: El 10 de noviembre, el investigador de IA Pietro Miotti compartió en X lo que parecía un antiguo centro cívico maya no cartografiado en México, hallado al pedir a decenas de agentes de IA que revisaran datos lidar públicos de la NASA. La publicación se volvió viral como "vibe archaeology" (arqueología vibe), impulsada por cuentas como Polymarket.

Pero el sitio no era un descubrimiento nuevo. Menos de un día después, Sarah Parcak, de la University of Alabama at Birmingham, señaló que lo habían documentado Francisco Estrada-Belli, de Tulane, y sus colegas en 2025. "Para esto existe la revisión por pares", dice Parcak. "No todo está en internet".

“Me parece genial que la gente quiera ser científica ciudadana usando IA y experimentar con ella”, dice Estrada-Belli. “Pero creo que no deberían aceptar los resultados a ciegas sin hacer comprobaciones de contexto o la debida diligencia antes de salir a hacer una afirmación así”.

Miotti corrigió sus publicaciones para reconocer el estudio. "Hoy una sola persona con una hipótesis puede poner a trabajar agentes de IA durante la noche para preseleccionar estructuras candidatas que evalúen los expertos", afirma, y añade que el episodio mostró la aportación humana: "revisión bibliográfica, verificación de campo y otros conocimientos especializados más específicos".

en.headline:
GPT-5.2 named the right species
in under 1 in 10 photos
en.body: Tested on 10,000 iNaturalist photos of Colombian vertebrates, GPT-5.2 reached only 9.5% species-level accuracy.

blocks.cap: Camera-trap image from the Morrocoy reserves: AI suggested Bassariscus sumichrasti; experts identified Metachirus myosuros. Credit: Fundación Sembrandopaz

blocks.x: A general-purpose AI model identified a marsupial caught by a camera trap in Colombia's Montes de María as Bassariscus sumichrasti, a species not known from Colombia, even though it was told where the animal was seen. Expert review confirmed it as Metachirus myosuros.

blocks.cap: Armadillo Cabassous centralis. Credit: Fundación Sembrandopaz

blocks.x: A study in the Biodiversity Data Journal by Gustavo Nicolas Paez Salamanca tested OpenAI's GPT-5.2 on 10,000 research-grade iNaturalist photos of Colombian amphibians, birds, fishes, mammals and reptiles, 2,000 per group. It reached 9.5% species-level accuracy: about 17–19% for mammals and reptiles, under 5% for amphibians, birds and fishes.

Species with fewer public photos and recently described species, such as the porcupine Coendou vossi, recognized in 2025, were harder. "If a rare animal is confused with a more familiar one, its presence might go unnoticed," Paez Salamanca says. cards.headline:
Ai2, Asta에
Theorizer 추가
cards.body: Theorizer는 논문 결과로 후보 이론을 세우고 주장마다 근거 논문을 단다.

blocks.x: Ai2가 과학 연구용 AI 에이전트 플랫폼 Asta에 Theorizer를 내놓고 코드도 오픈소스로 공개한다. Theorizer는 문헌을 검색한 뒤 논문마다 무엇을 뽑을지 템플릿을 만들고, 결과를 비교해 이론을 세운 다음 각 주장을 근거 논문과 잇는다.
Providence Swedish Cancer Institute의 Dr. Sid Devarakonda는 이를 "드라이버 음성(driver-negative)" 폐선암에 써 봤다. 첫 이론들을 검토하던 순간을 그는 이렇게 떠올렸다. "잠깐, 이건 정확히 내 생각과 같다. 이렇게 생각하기까지 나는 15년이 걸렸다."

blocks.cap: 알려진 유전적 드라이버 없이 자라는 폐선암을 설명하는 가능한 가설 세 가지.

blocks.x: Allen Institute의 Jérôme Lecoq는 한두 개를 예상했지만 Theorizer는 VIP 사이신경세포에 관한 후보 이론을 50개 내놓았다.

blocks.cap: 페루에서 최대 이슬점이 35°C를 넘은 셀. 그림: Piero Palacios, CIP.

blocks.x: International Potato Center에서는 틀렸지만 검증할 수 있는 설명 하나가 연구자들을 비현실적인 이슬점의 진짜 원인으로 이끌었다. Ai2는 Theorizer가 관련 연구를 놓치거나 독창성을 잘못 판단할 수 있다고 경고한다.

Dr. Sid Devarakonda of Providence Swedish Cancer Institute used it on "driver-negative" lung adenocarcinoma. Reviewing its first theories, he recalled: "Wait a second, this is exactly what I think. And it took me 15 years to think like this."

en.headline:
A proposed AI supertelescope
from three observatories
en.body: Astronomers propose using AI to fuse Rubin, Euclid and Roman pixels into a sharper virtual fourth observatory.

blocks.cap: ESA/Euclid/Euclid Consortium/NASA

blocks.x: Astronomers want to combine the Vera C. Rubin Observatory, the Euclid space telescope and the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope into a single AI-powered supertelescope. "Processed together, they make a fourth. And nobody has switched it on," says Gioia Rau of Renaissance Philanthropy.

In August Rau and more than two dozen co-authors released a preprint calling for action. With public investment already above $6 billion, the paper argues agencies should fund stitching the surveys together before the opportunity passes.

The goal is to "combine the pixels to get an image that is extremely high-resolution," says Rubin chief scientist Tony Tyson, aiding studies of dark energy, dark matter, supernovae and asteroids. "If we had 100 million volunteers, it would take us 120,000 years to annotate all of what the Rubin Observatory is acquiring," says Lior Shamir. "With AI, it's pretty instant."
"It has to be done," says Yale's Meg Urry. Roman is expected to begin its survey in early 2027.

Rubin首席科学家Tony Tyson说，目标是“把像素结合起来，得到分辨率极高的图像”，这将有助于暗能量、暗物质、超新星和小行星的研究。Lior Shamir说：“即使有1亿名志愿者，要为Rubin Observatory获取的全部数据做标注也需要120,000年。用AI的话，几乎是瞬间完成。”
Yale的Meg Urry说：“这件事必须做。”Roman预计将于2027年初开始巡天观测。

es.headline:
Propuesta de supertelescopio IA
a partir de tres observatorios
es.body: Astrónomos proponen usar IA para unir píxeles de Rubin, Euclid y Roman en un cuarto observatorio virtual más nítido.

blocks.cap: ESA/Euclid/Euclid Consortium/NASA

blocks.x: Los astrónomos quieren combinar el Vera C. Rubin Observatory, el telescopio espacial Euclid y el Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope en un único supertelescopio AI-powered (impulsado por IA). "Procesados juntos, forman un cuarto. Y nadie lo ha encendido", dice Gioia Rau, de Renaissance Philanthropy.

En agosto, Rau y más de dos docenas de coautores publicaron un preprint que pide actuar. Con una inversión pública que ya supera los 6.000 millones de dólares, el artículo sostiene que las agencias deberían financiar la integración de los sondeos antes de que pase la oportunidad.

El objetivo es "combinar los píxeles para obtener una imagen de altísima resolución", dice Tony Tyson, científico jefe de Rubin, lo que ayudaría a estudiar la energía oscura, la materia oscura, las supernovas y los asteroides. "Si tuviéramos 100 millones de voluntarios, tardaríamos 120.000 años en anotar todo lo que adquiere el Rubin Observatory", dice Lior Shamir. "Con IA, es prácticamente instantáneo".
"Hay que hacerlo", dice Meg Urry, de Yale. Se espera que Roman comience su sondeo a principios de 2027.
